questions.question: If the tool never judges whether code is correct, what is allowed to move a finding to "settled" (ball = nobody)?

options.label: Only a human/specialist act (Recommended)
options.description: Nothing the tool computes ever settles a code finding. Settlement requires an explicit act: the reviewer resolving the thread, a specialist sign-off, or a `rereview adjudicate` ruling. The tool's terminal state for a code finding is "change located — specialist's ball". Strongest and simplest; makes the safety property structural.

options.label: Split by type
options.description: Non-code types the tool CAN settle because no code judgment is involved — question answered+acknowledged, nit resolved at author discretion, praise-fyi. Code types (change-request, suggestion) always route to the specialist and never self-settle. Preserves useful automation where correctness isn't at stake.

options.label: Tool proposes, specialist confirms
options.description: The tool marks a finding "proposed settled" with the located change; it becomes settled only when a specialist or human confirms. Adds a state and a confirmation loop, but keeps a visible tool opinion.

questions.question: How strong is the correspondence claim the tool makes when it links a declaration to a code change?

options.label: Model-matched location, no adequacy claim (Recommended)
options.description: "Here is the change that appears to correspond to this declaration" — the model links declaration → specific hunks/lines, measured and allowed to abstain, explicitly making no claim that the change is correct, complete, or sufficient. The specialist decides adequacy.

options.label: Mechanical only — no model judgment
options.description: Purely deterministic: report which anchored files/lines changed after the declaration, and hand off. No model in the loop for correspondence at all. Maximum defensibility and cheapest, but much weaker signal on multi-file or moved-code fixes, which the corpus contains.

options.label: Location plus an advisory adequacy hint
options.description: As the recommended option, plus a non-binding "appears to fully address / appears partial / appears unrelated" hint for triage. Useful for prioritising the specialist's queue; risks being read as a verdict, so it would be rendered as an explicitly advisory signal.

questions.question: What is the handoff artifact, and does rereview decide WHICH specialized reviewer gets it?

options.label: Per-finding handoff lines + named domain (Recommended)
options.description: Each open finding emits a handoff line — declaration, its located change (file:line at head), and the domain it belongs to (repo-specific / architecture / security / performance / etc.) drawn from configurable domain rules. rereview names the domain but does not invoke anyone; a human or another agent picks it up.

options.label: One handoff brief, no routing
options.description: A single consolidated artifact listing every finding with its located change and current state. Simplest; leaves all triage and routing to whoever reads it.

options.label: Named domain AND configured reviewer identity
options.description: As the recommended option, plus per-domain configuration naming the actual reviewer (a GitHub handle, team, or agent/skill) so the handoff line says who owns it. More useful, but puts routing policy and identities into the tool's config surface.

options.label: rereview dispatches to the specialist agent
options.description: rereview actually invokes a configured specialized-reviewer skill/agent with the handoff payload. Most automated; a significant scope addition (outbound agent invocation) beyond v1's read-only-plus-one-comment posture.

questions.question: What happens to §9's evidence-scope apparatus — `nc`, class defaults, dependency-completeness — which exists to bound a correctness claim we'd no longer be making?

options.label: Keep re-check-on-change, drop correctness bounding (Recommended)
options.description: Retain the mechanism that re-locates a correspondence when the relevant files change again (a located change can go stale). Delete the dependency-completeness apparatus — `input-enumerated`/`not-proven`, security-class and global-invariant defaults, the negative-existence proof rules — since they bound a claim the tool no longer makes. Substantially simplifies §9 and §4.3.

options.label: Keep it, repurposed as location confidence
options.description: Retain the machinery but re-point it at correspondence quality: how completely the evidence builder enumerated what it searched when locating the change. Preserves the audit trail and the M3 class-flag metrics at the cost of keeping complexity whose original justification is gone.

options.label: Delete it entirely
options.description: Remove the evidence-scope apparatus including the re-check-on-change carry rules. Simplest, but loses the guard that a previously-located correspondence may no longer hold after later pushes.
